events.summary: President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that Fed Chair Jerome Powell ("Too Late") "should resign immediately", sharing an article about FHFA director William Pulte urging Congress to investigate Powell.
events.source_title: Trump says Fed Chair Jerome Powell 'should resign immediately' (Anadolu Agency, 3 Jul 2025)

events.summary: After media reports that Trump was likely to fire Powell, Trump said it was "highly unlikely unless he has to leave for fraud", referring to cost overruns in the $2.5bn renovation of Fed headquarters.
events.source_title: Trump repudiates draft letter to fire US Fed chair Powell (Al Jazeera, 16 Jul 2025)

events.summary: Trump announced he had fired Fed Governor Lisa Cook "for cause" over mortgage fraud allegations; Cook said no cause exists and sued on 28 Aug 2025. The D.C. Circuit (15 Sep 2025) and the Supreme Court (1 Oct 2025) refused emergency requests to remove her pending litigation.
events.source_title: Trump v. Cook (Wikipedia)

events.summary: Stephen Miran, chair of the White House Council of Economic Advisers, was sworn in as a Fed governor after a 48-47 Senate vote, filling Adriana Kugler's seat; he was the first Fed member to concurrently serve in the executive branch since the 1930s. He resigned from the CEA on 3 Feb 2026.
events.source_title: Stephen Miran (Wikipedia)

events.summary: The Department of Justice served the Federal Reserve with grand jury subpoenas threatening a criminal indictment related to Chair Powell's June 2025 Senate testimony on the renovation of Fed buildings. Powell said in a statement on 11 Jan 2026 that the action should be seen in the context of the administration's threats and pressure.
events.source_title: Statement from Federal Reserve Chair Jerome H. Powell (Federal Reserve Board, 11 Jan 2026)

events.summary: Kevin Warsh took office as Fed Chair for a term ending 21 May 2030, succeeding Jerome Powell, who chaired the Board from 5 Feb 2018 to 22 May 2026. Powell remains listed as a Board member.
events.source_title: Kevin Warsh, Chairman (Federal Reserve Board)

events.summary: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 in Trump v. Cook that Lisa Cook could remain on the Fed Board while her challenge to her removal proceeds, holding that the statute's for-cause protection entitles a governor to notice and an opportunity to respond.
events.source_title: Trump v. Cook (Wikipedia)

events.summary: The White House notified Lisa Cook that Trump was "considering" firing her and gave her three weeks to respond.
events.source_title: Trump v. Cook (Wikipedia)

events.summary: A presidential decree replaced central bank governor Murat Cetinkaya, whose term ran to 2020, with deputy Murat Uysal; Erdogan said Cetinkaya had made decisions for which a high price was paid, after the bank held its rate at 24%.
events.source_title: Turkey's Erdogan urges central bank overhaul: Report (Al Jazeera, 10 Jul 2019)

events.summary: President Erdogan removed governor Murat Uysal by decree in the Official Gazette and appointed former finance minister Naci Agbal, after the lira lost 30% of its value in 2020.
events.source_title: Turkey's Erdogan replaces central bank governor as lira plummets (Al Jazeera, 7 Nov 2020)

events.summary: Erdogan removed governor Naci Agbal by decree after four months in office, following an interest rate rise, and appointed Sahap Kavcioglu, a banking professor who had argued for lower rates.
events.source_title: Turkey's Erdogan sacks central bank governor after rate hike (Al Jazeera, 20 Mar 2021)

events.summary: Governor Sahap Kavcioglu, who had cut rates from 19% to 8.5%, was replaced by Hafize Gaye Erkan by presidential decree.
events.source_title: Şahap Kavcıoğlu (Wikipedia)

events.summary: President Bola Tinubu suspended Central Bank of Nigeria governor Godwin Emefiele with immediate effect, citing an ongoing investigation, and named Deputy Governor Folashodun Shonubi acting governor.
events.source_title: Emefiele Suspended, Shonubi Appointed Acting CBN Governor (ThisDay, 10 Jun 2023)

events.summary: The Tripoli-based Presidential Council issued a decree replacing Central Bank of Libya governor Sadiq al-Kabir, in post since October 2011, with former deputy governor Mohamed Abdul Salam al-Shukri.
events.source_title: Libya's presidential council replaces central bank governor (Arise News, 19 Aug 2024)

events.summary: Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah's government sent a delegation to take over the governor's office; al-Kabir said he and other senior staff fled the country because of militia threats, and banking operations were suspended.
events.source_title: Libya's central bank chief flees country over militia threats: Report (Al Jazeera, 30 Aug 2024)

events.summary: Bangladesh Bank governor Abdur Rouf Talukder resigned citing health reasons, four days after Sheikh Hasina fled the country and three days after more than a hundred central bank officials stormed his office demanding his resignation.
events.source_title: Bangladesh Bank governor resigns (The Daily Star, 9 Aug 2024)

events.summary: National Bank of Ukraine governor Yakiv Smolii submitted his resignation to President Zelensky, stating that "systematic political pressure has been exerted on the National Bank of Ukraine".
events.source_title: National Bank head Yakiv Smolii resigns due to political pressure (Kyiv Post)

events.summary: Central bank governor Tarek Amer, in office since 2015 with a term due to run to 2023, resigned; President al-Sisi accepted the resignation and named him a presidential adviser, with the pound at 19.1 to the dollar.
events.source_title: Egypt central bank chief quits amid deepening crisis (Al-Monitor/AFP, Aug 2022)

events.summary: President Hassan Rouhani's cabinet dismissed central bank governor Abdolnasser Hemmati because of his candidacy in the 18 June presidential election and replaced him with deputy Akbar Komijani.
events.source_title: Iran's central bank chief dismissed for running for president (Al Jazeera, 30 May 2021)

events.summary: President Edgar Lungu dismissed Bank of Zambia governor Denny Kalyalya, less than a week after he warned of economic difficulties, and appointed Christopher Mvunga from the finance ministry.
events.source_title: Zambian president fires central bank governor (Central Banking, 24 Aug 2020)

events.summary: Newly elected President Lazarus Chakwera dismissed Reserve Bank of Malawi governor Dalitso Kabambe and appointed Wilson Banda on 8 July 2020.
events.source_title: Malawi's new president dismisses governor (Central Banking)

events.summary: President Peter Mutharika appointed Henry Mathanga as Reserve Bank of Malawi deputy governor; Mathanga had been dismissed by the bank after a disciplinary inquiry and faces criminal charges, and critics say the appointment breaches Section 16(2) of the RBM Act.
events.source_title: Malawi: Outrage As Mutharika Appoints Fired and Charged Mathanga As RBM Deputy Governor (Nyasa Times via allAfrica, 11 Jan 2026)

events.summary: Sovereignty Council head Abdel Fattah al-Burhan dismissed Central Bank of Sudan governor Burai Al-Siddiq Ali Ahmed after a dispute over gold purchase and export rules and appointed Amna Mirghani Hassan El Toum; deputy governor Mohamed Osman Ahmed Mohamed Khair was dismissed less than two weeks later.
events.source_title: Sudan: Conflicts of Influence and Interests Confound Central Bank of Sudan (Dabanga via allAfrica, 29 Oct 2025)

events.summary: Three days after the 1 Feb 2021 coup, the military's State Administration Council appointed Than Than Swe deputy governor of the Central Bank of Myanmar; she later became governor, replacing Than Nyein.
events.source_title: Than Than Swe (Wikipedia)

events.summary: The junta replaced Central Bank governor Than Nyein and a vice chairman with Than Than Swe and Maj. Gen. Zaw Myint Naing, two months after appointing six lieutenant colonels as deputy directors.
events.source_title: Bank shake-up seen as bid by junta to control Myanmar's financial sector (RFA, 24 Aug 2022)

events.summary: After the Taliban takeover, the US froze nearly $9.5bn of Da Afghanistan Bank assets, much held at the New York Federal Reserve, and stopped cash shipments.
events.source_title: US freezes Afghan central bank's assets of $9.5bn (Al Jazeera, 18 Aug 2021)

events.summary: President Biden signed an executive order to split $7bn of frozen Afghan central bank assets: $3.5bn for Afghan relief and $3.5bn kept in the US for litigation by US victims of terrorism.
events.source_title: Biden moves to split $7 billion in frozen Afghan funds for 9/11 victims (AP via KTVU, 11 Feb 2022)

events.summary: After Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Western countries immobilised Russian central bank assets under their jurisdictions, estimated at around EUR 300bn worldwide.
events.source_title: Confiscation of immobilised Russian sovereign assets (European Parliamentary Research Service, 8 Sep 2025)

events.summary: The EU agreed to freeze EUR 210bn of Russian central bank assets held in Europe indefinitely, using Article 122 of the EU treaty, replacing six-monthly renewals that Hungary or Slovakia could veto.
events.source_title: EU agrees to indefinite freeze of Russian assets (Novaya Gazeta Europe, 13 Dec 2025)

events.summary: London's High Court ruled that Venezuelan supreme court judgments backing the Maduro-appointed central bank board should be disregarded, keeping more than $1bn of Venezuelan gold at the Bank of England out of Maduro's control.
events.source_title: London's High Court rules against Venezuela's Maduro in $1 billion gold battle (Reuters via Mining.com, 29 Jul 2022)

events.summary: Former central bank governor Riad Salameh, governor for three decades until 2023, was arrested in Beirut on charges of embezzlement, money laundering and fraud linked to commissions from the bank's dealings with a brokerage firm; he denies wrongdoing.
events.source_title: Former Lebanon central bank chief Riad Salameh arrested amid corruption probe (Semafor, 3 Sep 2024)

events.summary: Ruling-coalition MPs filed a motion to bring National Bank of Poland president Adam Glapiński before the State Tribunal on eight charges, including bond purchases that indirectly financed the budget deficit and unauthorised currency interventions.
events.source_title: Polish ruling coalition moves to put central bank governor on trial (Notes from Poland, 26 Mar 2024)

events.summary: The Sejm's Committee for Constitutional Responsibility backed a 148-page report upholding all eight charges against Glapiński, including PLN 144bn of bond purchases in 2020-21; a full Sejm vote must wait at least 21 days, and indictment could suspend him.
events.source_title: Tusk's parliamentary majority moves to depose head of Polish central bank (Brussels Signal, 12 Oct 2026)

events.summary: The National Bank of Hungary said a proposed government law widening the supervisory board's control over activities outside its basic tasks could erode its independence, amid pressure on Governor Gyorgy Matolcsy to cut rates.
events.source_title: Forint in 'perfect storm' as Hungary's central bank rebuffs law change (Reuters via Swissinfo, 12 Mar 2024)

events.summary: The government proposed amendments to the central bank law that would ban the MNB from creating new foundations, add a fourth deputy governor and expand the monetary policy committee from nine to 11 members.
events.source_title: Hungary to change central bank law (Central Banking, 14 May 2025)

events.summary: President Javier Milei announced a bill to reform the BCRA charter to restore a single mandate of preserving the currency's value, bar money issuance to finance the state and primary-market purchases of government bonds, and restrict profit transfers to the Treasury to debt repayment.
events.source_title: Cinco claves de la reforma del Banco Central y el 'grillete' fiscal impulsados por Milei (EFE via ABC Color, 30 Jul 2026)

events.summary: President Lula called central bank president Roberto Campos Neto his "political and ideological adversary" and said that when he could replace him at year-end Brazil would return "to normality".
events.source_title: Campos Neto é 'adversário político e ideológico', diz Lula (Poder360, 21 Jun 2024)

events.summary: President Gustavo Petro accused the Banco de la República of wanting to "finish off the economy" and of having an electoral bet after its board voted 4-3 to hold the rate at 9.25%.
events.source_title: Petro acusa al Banco de la República de tener una apuesta electoral (Publimetro, 31 Jul 2025)

events.summary: President López Obrador withdrew his nomination of former finance minister Arturo Herrera as Banco de México governor and nominated deputy finance secretary Victoria Rodríguez Ceja.
events.source_title: ¿Por qué AMLO retiró candidatura de Arturo Herrera al Banco de México? (Por Esto, 24 Nov 2021)

events.summary: Finance Minister Chris Sinckler fired Governor Delisle Worrell. The government's stated reason was that the board objected to his reported high-handed manner. Some observers believed the reason was his refusal to keep financing the government with new money: his January letter said the government must stop taking new money from the bank to pay its bills. The Appeals Court upheld the minister's right to dismiss him.
events.source_title: Barbados Central Bank governor fired (Caribbean Life)

events.summary: A junta court sentenced former deputy governor Bo Bo Nge to 20 years in prison in December 2022 after a months-long secret trial, sources said for "mismanagement of banks trading foreign currency". The junta-backed Anti-Corruption Commission accused him of not collecting tax on a $5 million Open Society deposit and of placing a $350 million loan in a lower-interest account, with alleged losses of 102, 360 and 655 million kyats. He was arrested on the morning of the February 2021 coup, and economist Sean Turnell called him someone "fighting against corruption".
events.source_title: Myanmar junta sentences former Central Bank official to 20 years in prison (RFA)
